raw_response:
I've been farming these 16.1 mu for five years now, and every year I learn something new—mostly from watching what my neighbors do and copying the ones who don't complain at harvest time. Last year I planted cotton on all of it using an improved variety I bought from the seed dealer in town after seeing Lao Zhang across the road get a good stand with it. I paid a bit more for the seeds, but his bolls were bigger, so I'm using the same kind this year. I need about 3 jin of seed per mu.

For fertilizer, I start from what I did last year and add a little, because losing yield scares me more than wasting a bag of fertilizer. At planting, I put down one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu—that's the 15-15-15 kind in the 50 kg bag. That's my base. Then when the cotton starts flowering, I spread 30 jin of urea per mu. Last year I also added another 20 jin of urea at the boll-filling stage, and I think that helped the top bolls get fatter, so I'm doing that again. The dealer says I could cut back, but my neighbor Aunt Wang puts down about the same and her cotton always looks greener than mine, so I'd rather spend the extra money. I hire Old Liu's tractor to do rotary tillage before planting—he charges about 40 yuan per mu, which is worth it because at 16.1 mu I can't do it all by hand, and plowing too deep around here just brings up salt.

I have my own well, so water isn't my biggest worry, but diesel for the pump is. I'll irrigate four times: right after sowing to get the seeds up, then at first flower, then at peak boll when the plants are drinking the most, and once more in late August if the weather stays dry. Cotton is thirsty when it's hot.

Pesticide is where I don't try to save money. The bollworm was bad three years ago and I lost half my top crop because I only sprayed five times. Last year I sprayed six times and still found some worms. This year I'm spraying seven times, starting when the squares show up and then every 10 to 15 days. Each spray costs me about 15 yuan per mu with the chemicals and hiring the sprayer, but one bad worm year is worse than seven sprays.

Last year I got about 500 jin of seed cotton per mu. This year, if the weather is decent and the worms don't beat me, I think I can get 550 jin per mu. With 16.1 mu, that should be enough to cover my costs and still have something left after feeding the six people in my house.
